tagline: A 1902 Belle Époque residence by the architect of the Peace Palace, on a former Carthusian monastery site in the heart of Saint-Émilion
highlights: Built from 1902 on the site of a former 18th-century Carthusian monastery once owned by Château Figeac
Designed by architect Louis-Marie Cordonnier, who also designed the Peace Palace in The Hague and the Lille Opera House
A member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World, set in a 7-acre park beside the Dordogne River
description:
Château Grand Barrail was built starting in 1902 on the site of a former 18th-century Bordeaux Carthusian monastery once owned by Château Figeac. Industrialist René Bouchart, a knight of the Legion of Honour, commissioned the building for his wife, Marie Godeau, hiring architect Louis-Marie Cordonnier — designer of the Peace Palace in The Hague and the Lille Opera House.

In 1992, new owners began restoring it into a hotel; it opened as a 4-star property in 1993. Today its 46 rooms and suites are spread across the château and its outbuildings, set in a 7-acre park beside the Dordogne River, roughly 3 km from Saint-Émilion village. It is a member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World.

The site's earlier history as a Carthusian monastery, once owned by the neighboring Château Figeac estate, connects Grand Barrail to Saint-Émilion's deep monastic and winemaking history, predating the current Belle Époque building by well over a century.

Architect Louis-Marie Cordonnier's involvement ties this Bordeaux château to a body of work that includes some of Europe's most significant civic buildings, an unusually prestigious architectural pedigree for a private residence of this scale.

The building's 1902 construction date makes it a genuinely different architectural period from the medieval fortresses found elsewhere in this collection — its appeal rests on Belle Époque grandeur and its Saint-Émilion vineyard setting rather than defensive castle history.

The surrounding Saint-Émilion wine appellation, a UNESCO World Heritage site for its medieval town and vineyard landscape, gives guests staying at Grand Barrail direct access to one of Bordeaux's most internationally recognized wine regions.

faqs.question: Is Château Grand Barrail a medieval castle?
faqs.answer: No — it's a Belle Époque residence built from 1902, on the site of a former 18th-century Carthusian monastery. The draw is its architecture and Saint-Émilion setting, not a defensive castle history.

faqs.question: Are all the rooms at Château Grand Barrail within the main building?
faqs.answer: No — the 46 rooms and suites are located in the château itself or its outbuildings, within the same 7-acre park.

faqs.question: How far is Château Grand Barrail from Saint-Émilion village?
faqs.answer: About 3 km, within the Saint-Émilion wine appellation and its UNESCO-listed medieval town.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** About 3 km from Saint-Émilion village, in the heart of the Saint-Émilion wine appellation; Bordeaux is roughly 40 minutes by car.

**Rooms & rates:** 46 rooms and suites from €200/night, split between the historic château and its outbuildings, set in a 7-acre park by the Dordogne River.

**On-site:** Spa with jacuzzi, two saunas, two hammams, a fitness room, gastronomic restaurant, and outdoor pool.

**Good to know:** A Belle Époque building (1902), not a medieval fortress — the draw here is the architecture and the Saint-Émilion vineyard setting rather than a defensive castle history.

**Combine with:** Saint-Émilion's UNESCO-listed medieval town and its wine estates, a short drive away.
